The first release of ParakeetRuntime.Net: offline speech-to-text for .NET on Windows. It runs NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 inside your process, on the CPU or a Direct3D 12 GPU, in 25 European languages. Audio never leaves the machine.

## What's in it

- **The `ParakeetRuntime.Net` NuGet package.** `SpeechModel` downloads and checks the 714 MB model once, `SpeechEngine` loads it and transcribes WAV files, streams or 16 kHz samples, and `Microphone` records into memory. Audio over 20 seconds is cut at its quietest points. Pure C#, no native runtime, no CUDA, no Python.
- **`parakeet-runtime.exe`**, a self-contained app: a page in the browser where you drop a WAV, the `transcribe`, `record` and `download` commands, and a local HTTP API on `127.0.0.1` that OpenAI-style clients can call.
- On the CPU it uses int8 kernels (AVX-VNNI-INT8, AVX-VNNI or AVX2). On a discrete GPU it runs the whole model as Direct3D 12 compute shaders. Integrated GPUs are used only when you name them, because the CPU beat them on both machines we measured.

## Speed

Against NVIDIA's NeMo-Speech.cpp on the same device, model (`parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.q8_0.gguf`) and FLEURS Polish and English clips of 20 seconds or less, with the same word error rate:

- Laptop, Core i7-11850H with a GeForce MX450, measured 2026-11-27 at this release's code: 1.0 s per minute of audio on the MX450 (1.7–1.8× NeMo) and 3.2–3.3 s on the CPU (3.7× NeMo).
- Desktop, Core Ultra 7 270K Plus with an RTX 5070 Ti, measured 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 on an earlier build: 2.1–2.3× NeMo on the GPU and 4.2–4.3× on the CPU.

Every run, with its command, is in [docs/benchmarks.md](https://github.com/kkolodziejczak/ParakeetRuntime.Net/blob/v0.5.0/docs/benchmarks.md).

## Downloads

- `ParakeetRuntime.Net-0.5.0-win-x64.zip`: `parakeet-runtime.exe`, no .NET installation needed.
- The `ParakeetRuntime.Net` 0.5.0 package on [nuget.org](https://www.nuget.org/packages/ParakeetRuntime.Net), also attached here.

Each file has a `.sha256` file next to it. `parakeet-runtime.exe`, `ParakeetRuntime.Net.dll` and the package are signed by **Open Source Developer Krzysztof Kołodziejczak** (certificate issued by Certum). Windows SmartScreen may still warn while the certificate builds reputation.
